title: Resume of studio hits: Four Seasons, Neil Sedaka, Connie Francis, Paul Anka
summary: At Hinton's urging he lists hit sessions, including the first bass drum mike on What's the Matter, Baby.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Congratulations. Say, look, you got such a magnificent resume here. I think it really should be read because I'm sure that the young people would want to know, or the people in the future would want to know some of the wonderful things that you have done and some things you've accomplished here, Panama. Would you like to read this and we'll just talk about it, because I think everybody should know about all of the -- especially these studio recordings; the hits you played on, just tell them some of the hits you played on. Just tell them.
Well, let's see; I made "Cindy, Oh Cindy" with Vince Vincent Martin.
Who was Vince Martin?
Vince Martin was a folk singer. I can't remember the fellow's name; he's a movie actor now, but he was also a member of the group.
Oh, it was a group? Vince Martin and the ...

Vince Martin, and this group. But I made "Cindy Oh Cindy," which was a big hit, and then I made "Goody, Goody" with Frankie Lyman, and I made "Summer Wind" with Wayne Newton, and I did "Big Girls Don't Cry," with the Four Seasons, and I did "Sherry," "Walk Like a Man," also the Four Seasons.
Were these done in New York?

Yeah, we recorded them in New York. I did "Prisoner of Love" with James Brown; I did "You're a Good Man, Charlie Brown," with the Kirby Stone Four, I did the "Colonel Boogie's March" with Mitch Miller; I did "Splash Splash" with Bobby Darin, I did "Calendar Girl" with Bobby Darin; I mean Neil Sedaka, I did Calendar Girl with.
Yeah, Neil is very hot now.
Yes, he is. He's a big star all over again.
we did quite a few thing with him down at RCA together, didn't we?
Yeah, that's right. Yeah, I think you were on "Calendar Girl," weren't you?
Yeah, I think so.
Yeah, and then I did "Stupid Cupid" with Connie Francis; also, "Who's Sorry Now?" I did "Venus" with Frankie Avalon, and "From Bobby Socks to Stockings."
These were all hit records?

All these were hit records. I did Fabian's first hit record, "Like a Tiger." And I did "These Things Remind Me of You" with Della Reese; I did "Haunting Melody" with Sarah Vaughn, which is the only million selling record she ever made; I did, "What's the Matter, Baby," with [Timmie Yuro.]
Yeah, from California. I think I was on that, too.
Yeah, with Clyde Otis.
Yeah, Clyde Otis. Right.
At the Fine Sounds.
Yeah, the Fine Sounds Studio. It's not even there any more; the hotel is gone.

That's right. And the arrangement with Burt Keith. That's the first time that they used a mike on a bass drum. Was on that record. "What's The Matter, Baby?" That's when they put the mike on the bass drum, was on that record.
Huh? Is that so?

Yeah, on "What's The Matter, Baby." That's it. And I did "Lonely Boy" with Paul Anka and "You Are My Destiny" with Paul Anka, and "Patricia," which we spoke about earlier; I told you how I suggested to set up the rhythm on the overdub.
